fail-closed park. At ~67KB/s while a position is open, a fresh file passes 1MiB
~16 seconds into the first trade => any kill/restart after that parks the strategy.

5. MECE class sweep — not just this instance: for EVERY dedupe key in the #1356

   stable-categorical vs tick-flappable (clock races, threshold hovering, jitter).
   rv_gate_result in ExitOutcomeKey is the proven flapper. Evidence per field, not

6. Design proposal with alternatives considered. Hard constraints:

   - If the right fix is gate semantics (how future-dated is classified), that is a

content.text: The behavioral trace already shows the flap is not “evidence-only”: `RejectedFutureDated` removes RV from the shared pricing state. Entry returns `RealizedVolNotReady`; exit loses hold EV and therefore defaults to `Hold`. The observed session happened to remain `Hold` on accepted ticks too, but that masks a live decision discontinuity rather than making it harmless.

The historical review trail matters here: #1180 explicitly recorded “one `VenueEventMs` across different venues” as a real skew mechanism, and #1275 still tracks it. #1204 then treated all venue-event stamps as one comparable domain; the real A↔B flood is the missing production proof that invalidates that ruling. I’m also updating the census to current `v0.1.12`: #1351 added `terminal_settlement` after #1356, so the authoritative current count is 20 structural append paths, not 19.

Correction after tracing the new writer: #1351 did not increase the reachable count. It replaced the production `settlement_booking_error` append with canonical `terminal_settlement`; the legacy writer/reader remains for compatibility but has no production caller. So the current exhaustive table is still 19 reachable paths, with that row substituted.

The field census shows #1356’s “categorical-only” conclusion was too strong even beyond `rv_gate_result`: all four strategy dedupe keys contain at least one live-state field that can oscillate, while the maker requote key is bounded by a per-episode history set. Only the RV gate field has a measured production flood today; the others need their risk classification corrected without broadening this fix’s implementation scope.

## Phase 1 ruling report

Recommendation: fix RV admission semantics in the shared pricing layer. The current gate compares timestamps from independently clocked venues that merely share the `VenueEventMs` Rust type. Removing `rv_gate_result` from the evidence key or adding a history-set dedupe would hide a real pricing discontinuity.

Phase 2 has not started. No issue, branch, test, commit, PR, or file change was made.

### 1. Behavioral impact and complete caller census

There are exactly two production calls to `classify_rv_gate`:

1. The behavioral admission path in [bolt_v3_fair_value_pricing.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_fair_value_pricing.rs:362). It admits the snapshot only for `Accepted`; every other result becomes `None`.
2. The taker evidence wrapper in [bolt_v3_taker_pricing.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_taker_pricing.rs:363), consumed at:

   - exit log/evidence field construction: [mod.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:5607)
   - durable `exit_evaluation`: [mod.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:6715)

The classifier and its unit callers are in [bolt_v3_fair_value_pricing.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_fair_value_pricing.rs:443).

Behavioral consumers:

- Entry: rejected RV becomes `RealizedVolNotReady`; entry evaluation returns before fair probability, sizing, or submission. There is no degraded price and no prior-snapshot fallback. The same stored snapshot can be accepted on the next tick. See [entry pricing](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:3724) and [entry evaluation](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:7138).
- Normal exit: rejected RV makes fair probability and `hold_ev_bps` unavailable. `evaluate_exit_decision` then returns `Hold`; accepted RV performs the real hold-vs-exit comparison. See [hold-EV construction](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:5273), [exit evaluation](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:5411), and [missing-input Hold](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/exit_decision.rs:348).
- Forced-flat exit is unaffected because it returns `Exit` before RV valuation.
- `position_interval_ended` is also decided before RV valuation. In that phase the flap is evidence-only, but during `exit_hold` it is behaviorally live.
- Maker pricing uses the same shared gate. A rejection blocks the entire maker fair-value decision as `RealizedVolNotReady`: [bolt_v3_maker_runtime_quote.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_maker_runtime_quote.rs:153).

Therefore the measured session’s unchanged `Hold` result masks the behavior change only for that dataset. Structurally, the accepted half can compute an exit while the rejected half is forced to hold.

### 2. Why venue-event time was chosen, and why that ruling failed

[#1180](https://github.com/seungpyoson/bolt-v2/pull/1180) moved RV `as_of_ms` from receive/strategy time to venue-event time to preserve replayable event truth and prevent local-vs-event comparisons. [#1204](https://github.com/seungpyoson/bolt-v2/pull/1204) then passed the consuming trigger’s venue-event timestamp, treating both sides as one domain.

That was intended to provide deterministic replay, same-domain freshness, and fail-closed handling for local/unknown triggers. The defect is that `VenueEventMs` distinguishes venue time from local time but does not distinguish one venue/source clock from another: [bolt_v3_timestamp_domain.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_timestamp_domain.rs:12).

The RV surface clock is the maximum event timestamp across sources—including rejected-event timestamps—and publication preserves the maximum: [bolt_v3_realized_volatility.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_realized_volatility.rs:461), [bolt_v3_realized_volatility_runtime.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/bolt_v3_realized_volatility_runtime.rs:386). A Polymarket book event is therefore being strictly ordered against an aggregate Binance/Bybit-style event watermark. The type system permits it, but the clocks are independent.

This was already recorded as a real mechanism during #1180 review and remains item 20 in [#1275](https://github.com/seungpyoson/bolt-v2/issues/1275). The production A↔B measurement is the missing evidence that invalidates #1204’s approval.

### 3. `position_id=None` flood-guard path

The path is reachable, but not as a repeating tick writer at current `main`.

All production callers check for a managed position before calling exit evaluation:

- selection update: [mod.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:975)
- signal quote: [mod.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:1552)
- book delta: [mod.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:7638)

Inside the invocation, a missing-interval terminal settlement can durably release the position before the exit decision is assembled: [mod.rs](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:6577), [terminal transition](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/mod.rs:1367). That produces one unkeyed exit-evaluation record; exposure is then `Flat`, preventing subsequent exit calls.

Conclusion: reachable and ungated, but structurally one-shot—not a current per-tick flood path. Phase 2 should add a reachability regression, but no recording cap/fence is warranted.

### 4. Dedupe-key field census

| Key | Stable-categorical fields | Tick-flappable fields | Churn conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BlockedStrategyInputDedupeKey` | target/ruleset/market/instrument/surface/source IDs; sorted source order; unknown-source ID set | blocker vectors, selected side, availability/incoherence/failover, RV status/block reason/last reject reason | Last-key A→B→A vulnerable in principle. Real replay: 8/125,143 survivors, zero oscillation. Empirically quiet, not categorical-only by construction. |
| `EntrySkipDedupeKey` | market ID; interval strike after its one-time bind | reason category, gate/pricing blockers, venue/reference availability, incoherence | Last-key A→B→A vulnerable at book cadence. Churn unmeasured; cannot be globally safety-cleared. |
| `ExitDecisionDedupeKey` | market ID, position ID | forced-flat reasons, Hold/Exit result, blocked reason | Last-key vulnerable. Book availability, health predicates, and hold/exit threshold hovering can oscillate. |
| `ExitOutcomeKey` | none beyond the position-scoped map key | exit decision, submission block, RV gate result | Proven flood: 40,442/40,849 A→B→A flips, 43.49 records/sec. |
| `RequoteThrottleDedupeKey` | family, leg, sole block-reason category | action-cost class and sliding-window `bound_by` | Fields flap, but the implementation retains every encountered key until unblock. Continuous A→B→A is bounded by the finite enum product per episode. |

Definitions: [entry keys](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/entry_decision.rs:260), [exit keys](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_edge_taker/exit_decision.rs:185), [requote key](/Users/spson/Projects/Claude/bolt-v2/src/strategies/binary_oracle_maker/mod.rs:134).

The #1356 claim that existing keys contain only categorical state is therefore false. Some dynamic fields represent genuine behavior transitions and should remain; the error was treating “no timestamps/prices” as equivalent to “cannot churn.”

### 5. Current 19-path sweep

The [#1356 table](https://github.com/seungpyoson/bolt-v2/pull/1356) remains complete at 19 reachable paths, with one current-main substitution: #1351 replaced the production `settlement_booking_error` append with canonical `terminal_settlement`. The legacy writer/reader remains for compatibility but has no production caller.

| Path | Current churn classification |
|---|---|
| blocked `strategy_input_snapshot` | Last-key state observation; latent flappers, measured quiet |
| submit `strategy_input_snapshot` | Client-order event |
| `order_intent` | Submit/action event |
| `admission_decision` | Admission event |
| `basket_admission_decision` | Basket action event |
| `capital_admission_rebuild` | Startup lifecycle event |
| `submit_reservation_metadata` | Reservation event |
| `submit_reservation_fill` | Fill/trade event |
| `entry_skip` | Last-key state observation; latent flappers |
| `exit_decision` | Last-key state observation; latent flappers |
| `exit_evaluation` | Last-key state observation; proven RV-gate flood |
| `loss_governor_halt` | Episode/power-of-two sampling; bounded |
| `order_reject` | Real reject or sampled episode event |
| `order_lifecycle` | Lifecycle transition event |
| `requote_throttle` | Finite per-episode history set |
| `settlement` | Durable settlement-key event |
| `terminal_settlement` | Canonical settlement-key terminal event |
| `venue_truth_capture_failure` | Ungated periodic failure writer with no named reader; separate unresolved flood risk |
| `venue_truth_divergence` | Durable halt event |

No separate strategy/live-node disk appender was found. The current writer trait has 19 methods, and the direct-appender sweep returned zero matches.

This means Phase 2 may claim the measured `exit_evaluation` flood fixed, but must not claim every possible #1354 writer flood is closed while `venue_truth_capture_failure` remains periodic and ungated.

### 6. Design alternatives

Decision: which clock owns RV consumption freshness?

Invariant: RV admission must not depend on relative ordering between independent venue clocks, while genuinely stale RV must still fail closed using the existing configured source-age policy.

#### Option A — causal receive-time freshness in the pricing layer (recommended)

Approach:

- Give each ready RV snapshot a typed freshness watermark derived from the latest accepted contributing observation’s receive/init timestamp.
- Rejected observations must not refresh it, also closing the adjacent poison-timestamp mechanism tracked by #1275.
- Compare that watermark to the consumer’s receive/init timestamp using saturating age and the existing `max_source_age_ms`.
- No strict cross-venue “future” rejection. Retain `RejectedFutureDated` only for historical evidence decoding.
- Keep venue `as_of_ms` for RV computation and RCA, but stop using it as an admission clock.
- Pass receive-domain evaluation context through all shared pricing consumers:

  - entry book trigger
  - exit signal/book trigger
  - maker selected reference quote
  - local/selection triggers without receive time remain `MissingEvaluationEventTime → Hold`

- Persist the receive watermark and computed age in exit evidence. Keep the venue-event delta as diagnostic only.

Upside: removes the actual cross-source race, retains deterministic replay because `ts_init` is recorded input, detects dead streams without new thresholds, and is venue-agnostic.

Downside: changes the shared snapshot/pricing contract and evidence schema; more fixtures and call sites move.

Blast radius if wrong: entry may admit, normal exit may choose Exit, and maker pricing may quote on ticks previously blocked. This is explicitly a pricing-layer behavior change.

#### Option B — saturating venue-event age

Delete the strict future check and treat `snapshot.as_of > trigger_event` as age zero.

Upside: small patch and stops this 94ms flap.

Downside: preserves the false “all venues share one clock” model; far-future or rejected timestamps can keep a snapshot apparently fresh. It does not close #1275’s multi-venue/poison class.

Verdict: reject.

#### Option C — evidence-only treatment

Remove `rv_gate_result` from `ExitOutcomeKey`, or remember all observed outcomes per position.

Upside: immediately bounds disk writes.

Downside: RV admission still flickers; entry, exit, and maker behavior remains discontinuous. This silences the symptom and violates the brief.

Verdict: reject.

### 7. Proposed Phase 2 proof

If Option A is approved, the differential red proof should alternate book-trigger event clocks around one unchanged ready RV snapshot while holding exit decision and block reason constant. Pre-fix, six A→B ticks should emit six `exit_evaluation` records; the post-fix expectation is one.

Additional required differentials:

- entry remains RV-admitted across benign cross-source event skew;
- normal-exit hold EV does not disappear as trigger venue stamps alternate;
- maker fair value remains admitted under the same skew;
- receive-age beyond configured `max_source_age_ms` still rejects stale;
- rejected/future-poison event stamps do not refresh the causal watermark;
- missing receive context remains fail-closed;
- terminal-release `position_id=None` produces at most one record.

Phase 2 would then search issues—including #1275 item 20—file the mandated issue with #1354 as class parent, use `fix/NNNN-exit-evaluation-rv-gate-flood`, and follow the requested red/full-unfiltered/exact-head verification protocol.

Verification for this phase: remote `main`, local `main`, `origin/main`, and `HEAD` all equal `9ac211fe121b7b825a5f4da8e7590e00d2b3c90b`; the worktree and diff are clean. No Rust suite was run because Phase 1 made no code changes.

Ruling requested: approve or reject Option A. I will not begin Phase 2 without the explicit ruling.

ADDENDUM to the exit_evaluation flood brief — supersedes where it conflicts.

1. ISSUE: do NOT file a new issue. #1354 has been REOPENED (closure disproven by the
   deploy-day histogram) — work under it and read its latest comment first: it carries
   the full evidence chain. Branch: fix/1354-rv-gate-clock-domain.

2. ROOT-CAUSE REFINEMENT: a prior fix already stopped comparing venue time against
   local-machine time. The remaining defect is that classify_rv_gate still treats
   event timestamps from DIFFERENT venues as directly comparable (RV snapshot as_of =
   spot-source venue clock; gate event time = consuming venue's book clock; they lead
   each other by milliseconds). Frame the investigation as a clock-domain ownership
   problem, not a jitter/tolerance problem.

3. PHASE 1, two additions:
   a. REPLAY: reconstruct classify_rv_gate inputs from the archived session records and
      confirm the flip reproduces through current v0.1.12 code from cross-venue
      timestamp comparison alone.
   b. RECOVERY-CAPACITY PROOF (mandatory): recompute the captured session's evidence
      volume as it WOULD be with the fix applied (legitimate state transitions only);
      derive legitimate growth per hour of open-position time. If legitimate evidence
      still exceeds the 1MiB whole-file recovery limit before a planned restart in a
      24h soak, state so explicitly — segmented recovery/rotation then becomes an
      additional pre-soak requirement under #1275/#763. Show the arithmetic.

4. RULING ENVELOPE (fixed in advance): the fix is timestamp ownership at the pricing
   layer — comparisons only within one clock domain, enforced by the owning types, not
   patched at a call site. NO tolerance windows, NO rate caps, NO sampling, NO raising
   recovery_evidence_max_bytes. If your census says this envelope is wrong, argue it
   in the Phase-1 proposal; do not implement outside it.

5. PHASE 2 SCOPE: the proven root cause ONLY. The MECE dedupe-key sweep and the
   position_id=None guard-bypass audit remain Phase-1 deliverables, but their findings
   are REPORTED on #1354 — not fixed in this PR. No bundling.

6. TESTS: in addition to the RED/GREEN differential, prove restart recovery with an
   open position BOTH below and above the 1MiB boundary.

7. PROCESS: exact-head remote full CI, external review, required approval, merge queue.
   No manual CI dispatches.

I’ll treat the addendum as the new Phase 1 scope and remain read-only with respect to repository code. I’m using the same systematic-diagnosis and planning workflows to (1) read #1354’s newest evidence chain, (2) replay archived `exit_evaluation` inputs through exact v0.1.12 logic, and (3) calculate post-fix recovery capacity before revising the ruling proposal.
